brief: Explain how accounts payable confirms the settlement network on a USDT or USDC invoice before release. titleDe: When a crypto invoice counts as paid: confirmation rules finance can defend
titleEn: When a crypto invoice counts as paid: confirmation rules finance can defend
unsplashQuery: accountant reviewing invoice status on screen
brief: Define practical rules for marking a B2B crypto invoice paid. Cover who checks the transaction hash or desk ticket, what confirmation or desk status counts, how a network fee can leave the received amount short of paid-in-full, and how the status is written back to the AP ledger. This is an accounts-payable control, not a blockchain theory piece and not a how-to for reconciling overpayments.

titleDe: Network fee responsibility on B2B crypto invoices: who funds the shortfall
titleEn: Network fee responsibility on B2B crypto invoices: who funds the shortfall

Cover payer-pays versus receiver-pays, topping up a shortfall, and the fee line accounting needs. Stay on the fee rule. Do not turn the article into a general partial-payment or overpayment reconciliation guide.

titleDe: Credit notes after stablecoin settlement: reversing a paid crypto invoice
titleEn: Credit notes after stablecoin settlement: reversing a paid crypto invoice
brief: Walk through a commercial credit note or refund after an invoice was already settled in USDT or USDC. Cover a return transfer, a credit against the next invoice, and a desk ticket, plus the references that tie the credit to the original payment and the evidence accounting files. Do not promise that a wrong-wallet transfer can be reversed, and do not give tax advice.

titleDe: Segregating operating stablecoins from reserves: a treasury wallet map
titleEn: Segregating operating stablecoins from reserves: a treasury wallet map
brief: Explain a wallet map that separates stablecoins funding this week’s payables from longer-term treasury reserves. Cover named owners, spend limits, and how a payable run draws only from the operating balance. This is policy and operations. Do not review custody products, do not size a liquidity buffer, and do not discuss trading mandates.

titleDe: Intercompany stablecoin settlement: documenting transfers between group entities
titleEn: Intercompany stablecoin settlement: documenting transfers between group entities

brief: Describe how two legal entities in one group settle an intercompany invoice in a stablecoin. Cover a wallet per entity, the internal invoice as the source document, who approves the transfer, and how both ledgers record the same hash or desk ticket. Do not discuss tax consolidation or moving assets as an investment between entities.

titleDe: Month-end tie-out for stablecoin balances: a controller checklist
titleEn: Month-end tie-out for stablecoin balances: a controller checklist

Cover which wallet view or provider statement to use, how to treat in-flight hashes and unfilled desk tickets at cut-off, and how this period close differs from the per-payment evidence pack produced during the month. Do not give valuation advice or claim a specific accounting-standard outcome.

titleDe: Off-ramping stablecoin receipts to the operating account: timing and evidence
titleEn: Off-ramping stablecoin receipts to the operating account: timing and evidence
brief: Explain the operations path when a customer pays a B2B invoice in USDT or USDC and treasury converts that receipt into fiat in the operating account. Cover quote timing, who approves the conversion, how the inbound hash and the fiat credit are linked, and what stays open if conversion settles after month-end. Do not frame holding the receipt as an investment decision.

titleDe: Test transfer before a supplier crypto payout: amount, network, and sign-off
titleEn: Test transfer before a supplier crypto payout: amount, network, and sign-off

titleEn: Hybrid settlement day: aligning bank cut-offs with on-chain release

titleEn: Stablecoin clauses in supplier contracts: asset, network, tolerance, and fees

titleDe: Remittance advice after a crypto supplier payment: what to send with the hash
titleEn: Remittance advice after a crypto supplier payment: what to send with the hash

titleDe: Sanctions rescreening for repeat crypto payees: cadence, triggers, and evidence
titleEn: Sanctions rescreening for repeat crypto payees: cadence, triggers, and evidence

titleEn: Record retention for crypto payment files: what the evidence pack should keep

titleEn: Source-of-funds pack for business stablecoin buys: documents treasury should file

titleEn: Compliance hold before a crypto payable release: pause, review, and restart
